title: Transfer Case Service
summary: Maintenance blueprint for checking transfer case fluid condition, AWD/4WD interval needs, leaks, and engagement concerns before fluid service.
symptoms: AWD/4WD transfer case service interval due
Fluid dark, low, burnt, contaminated, or unknown history
Case seepage at output seals, drain/fill plugs, or case seams
4WD engagement noise, binding, or actuator concern requiring diagnosis first
inspect_first: Transfer case fluid specification and service interval
Fluid level, color, smell, debris, and water contamination
Input/output seals, case vent, drain/fill plugs, and mounting condition
4WD/AWD engagement behavior, actuator codes, and tire size matching concerns
repair_overview: Confirm transfer case type, fluid specification, and fill procedure.
Remove fill plug first where applicable, then inspect fluid level and condition.
Drain fluid, inspect plug magnet and debris, then refill to the correct level.
Check for leaks, verify vent condition, and road test or cycle AWD/4WD modes when applicable.
Document any actuator, binding, tire mismatch, or noise concern that needs diagnosis.
common_mistakes: Using ATF or gear oil when the transfer case requires a specific fluid
Skipping fill-plug access check before draining
Treating actuator or binding complaints as fluid maintenance only
Missing tire size mismatch or driveline windup on AWD/4WD systems
estimate_guidance: Quote the correct transfer case fluid and fill procedure for the vehicle.
Flag seized fill plugs, skid plate access, and seal leaks as labor variables.
Recommend diagnosis before service when engagement faults, binding, or codes are present.
Suggest differential service only when interval, fluid condition, or drivetrain context supports it.

specialty: Transfer case fill adapter where required
Scan tool for 4WD/AWD actuator checks when needed

diagnostic_context.intro: Transfer case service is maintenance when fluid condition and interval support it; AWD/4WD engagement faults still need diagnosis.
